translations.text: These are the words of the book that Baruch son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah, son of Zedekiah, son of Hassadiah, son of Hilkiah, wrote in Babylon,
in the fifth year, on the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans captured Jerusalem and burned it with fire.
Baruch read the words of this book in the hearing of Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and in the hearing of all the people who came for the book,

and in the hearing of the soldiers and the kings’ sons, and in the hearing of the elders, and in the hearing of all the people, from the least to the greatest, everyone who lived in Babylon by the river Sud.
They wept and fasted and prayed before the Lord.
They collected silver, each according to his ability,
and sent it to Jerusalem, to the priest Joakim son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum, and to the other priests who were with him in Jerusalem.

This was when he received the vessels of the Lord’s house that had been taken out of the temple, to return them to the land of Judah, on the tenth day of the month of Sivan—the silver vessels that Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, had made,

after Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians, had taken captive Jeconiah, the rulers, the prisoners in chains, the warriors, and the people of the land from Jerusalem, and had brought them to Babylon.
They said, “Look, we have sent you silver. With this silver buy burnt offerings, sin offerings, and incense, and prepare manna and offer it on the altar of the Lord our God.
Pray for the life of Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians, and for the life of Belshazzar his son, so that their days on earth may be like the days of heaven.

May the Lord give us strength and enlighten our eyes, so that we may live under the protection of Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians, and under the protection of Belshazzar his son, and serve them for many days and find favor before them.
Pray also for us to the Lord our God, for we have sinned against the Lord our God, and the Lord’s indignation and anger have not turned away from us to this day.
Read this book, which we have sent you to place in the Lord’s house, on feast days and at the appointed times.
And say: ‘Righteousness belongs to the Lord our God, but shame belongs to us, as it does this day—to the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
and to our kings, our rulers, our priests, our prophets, and our fathers before the Lord.
For we disobeyed him and did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God, to walk according to the Lord’s commandments that he set before us.
From the day when the Lord brought our fathers out of the land of the Egyptians until this day, we have been disobedient to the Lord our God and have avoided listening to his voice.

The calamities and the curse that the Lord decreed through Moses his servant have overtaken us, as they have this day—the curse decreed on the day when he brought our fathers out of the land of the Egyptians to give us the land flowing with milk and honey.
We did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God, according to all the words of the prophets whom he sent to us.
Instead, each of us followed the thoughts of his own evil heart, paying tribute to foreign gods and doing evil before the Lord our God.
The Lord fulfilled the words that he spoke against us and against our judges who judged Israel, and against our kings, our rulers, and the people of Israel and Judah,
bringing upon us great calamities such as had never been brought about anywhere under heaven, as he did to Israel, according to what is written in the Law of Moses.
for us to eat the flesh of our sons, and for a man to eat the flesh of his daughter
And he handed us over into slavery to all the kings around us, to be a reproach and a desolation among all the surrounding peoples, wherever the Lord scattered us.
And we were brought low, not raised high, because we sinned against the Lord our God by not listening to his voice.
Righteousness belongs to the Lord our God, but shame belongs to us and our fathers, as it does this day,
which the Lord pronounced against us—all these calamities that have come upon us.
And we did not plead before the Lord, each of us turning away from the evil thoughts of his own heart.
And the Lord kept watch over the calamities that the Lord stirred up against us, for the Lord is righteous in all his works that he commanded us.
And we did not listen to his voice, to follow the commands of the Lord that he set before us.

And now, Lord God of Israel, who brought your people out of the land of the Egyptians with a mighty hand, with signs and wonders, with great acts of power and an uplifted arm, and made a name for yourself, as it is to this day:
We have sinned, acted wickedly, and done wrong, Lord our God, against all your ordinances.
Let your wrath turn away from us, for we are left few in number among the nations where you scattered us.
Hear, Lord, our prayers and our petitions, and save us for your name’s sake, and grant us favor before our captors.
So that the whole earth may know that you are the Lord our God, for your name has been called upon Israel and upon his people.
Lord, look down from your holy temple and consider us. Incline your ear, Lord, and hear.
Open your eyes and see, for the dead in Hades, whose spirits have been taken away, will not give glory and righteousness to the Lord.
But souls grieving in unbearable sorrow, who walk bowed down and sick, with dim eyes and hungry souls, will give you glory and righteousness.
Lord, it is not because of the righteous deeds of our fathers and our kings that we lay our pleas for mercy before you, Lord our God.
For you brought your wrath and your anger upon us, just as you spoke through your servants the prophets, saying:
“Thus says the Lord: Bow your necks and pay tribute to the king of the Babylonians, and dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers.”
And if you do not listen to the voice of the Lord and pay tribute to the king of the Babylonians, I will bring decline to the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem.
the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride; and the whole land will become a wilderness without inhabitants.

And we did not listen to your voice and pay tribute to the king of the Babylonians. And you fulfilled your words that you spoke through your servants the prophets, that the bones of our kings and the bones of our fathers would be taken out of their resting places.
And behold, they lie exposed to the heat of the day and the cold of the night; and they died in terrible suffering, by famine, by the sword, and in captivity.
And you made your temple, upon which your name was called, as it is this day, because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
And you dealt with us, Lord our God, according to all your gentleness and all your great compassion,
as you spoke through your servant Moses on the day when you commanded him to write your law before the children of Israel,
and to say: “If you do not listen to my voice, surely this great and mighty throng will become small among the nations where I scatter you.”
For I know that they will not listen to me, because they are a stiff-necked people. But they will turn their hearts in the land of their exile.
And they will know that I am the Lord their God, and I will give them a heart and ears to listen.
And they will bless me in the land of their captivity and remember my name.
And they will turn away from their stubbornness and their evil deeds, for they will remember the ways of their ancestors who sinned before me.
And I will bring them back to the land that I swore to give to their ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. They will possess it, and I will multiply them, and they will not diminish.
And I will establish an everlasting covenant with them: I will be their God, and they will be my people. And I will no longer uproot my people Israel from the land that I gave them.
Lord Almighty, God of Israel, afflicted souls and weary spirits cry out to you.
Hear, Lord, and have mercy, for you are a merciful God. Have mercy, for we have sinned before you.
For you dwell forever, but we perish forever.

Lord Almighty, God of Israel, hear the prayers of the dead of Israel and of their children who sinned before you, who did not listen to the voice of the Lord their God, so that calamities surrounded us.
Do not remember the sins of our ancestors, but remember your hand and your name at this time.
For you are the Lord our God, and we will bless you, Lord.

For this reason you put the fear of you into our hearts, so that we might call upon your name. And we will bless you in our captivity, for we have taken to heart all the wrongdoing of our ancestors who sinned before you.
Look, today we are in our captivity, where you scattered us, to suffer reproach, curses, and penalties, according to all the lawless deeds of our ancestors who rebelled against the Lord our God.
Hear, Israel, the commandments of life; listen so that you may know wisdom.
What is it, Israel? Why are you in the land of enemies?
You have grown old in a foreign land; you have mingled with corpses; you have been counted among those who have gone down to the underworld.
You have abandoned the land of wisdom.
If you had walked in the way of God, you would have dwelt in peace forever.
Learn where wisdom is, where strength is, where understanding is, so that you may also know what long life is, and where the light of the eyes and peace are.
Who has found her dwelling place, and who has entered her treasuries?
Where are the rulers of the nations and those who ruled over the beasts of the earth,
who soared with the birds of heaven,
and stored up silver and gold in which people trusted? There was no limit to their possessions. And where are those who work silver and gold and take pains, whose works cannot be fathomed?
They perished and went down to the underworld, and others arose in their place.
Young men saw the light and lived on the earth, but they did not know the ways of wisdom.
They did not consider her paths, and their children did not remain upon her path; they stayed far from her way.
It was not heard of in Canaan, nor was it seen in Teman.
Nor did the sons of Hagar seek wisdom. The merchants of Merran and Teman, the storytellers and the investigators of wisdom, did not know the way of wisdom, nor did they remember its paths.
O Israel, how great is the house of God, and how spacious is the place of his possessions!
It is great and without limit, lofty and immeasurable.
There were born the renowned giants who existed from the beginning, mighty and skilled in warfare.
God did not choose them, nor did he give them the way of wisdom.
And they perished for lack of wisdom and were destroyed because of their own foolishness.
Who has gone up to heaven and taken it, and brought it down from the clouds?
Who has crossed to the other side of the sea and found it, and could bring it in exchange for the finest gold?
There is no one [?] who knows its ways, nor anyone who can bring its paths to mind.
But the one who knows everything knows it; he found it through his own wisdom. The one who established the earth for all time filled it with animals and four-footed creatures.
He sends out the light, and it goes; he called it, and it obeyed him with trembling.
The stars shone, each at its own watch, and rejoiced.
He called them, and they said, “Here we are!” They shone with joy for their Creator.
This is our God; no other can be reckoned alongside him.
He found all the ways of wisdom and gave it to Jacob his servant and to Israel, whom he loved.
After this, he appeared on earth and walked among human beings.
These are the books of God's commandments and the laws that remain forever. All who receive it will live, and those who abandon it will die.
Turn back, Jacob, and take hold of it, in the radiance before its light.
Do not give your glory to another, nor your benefit to a foreign nation.
Blessed are we, Israel, because we know what is pleasing to God.
Take courage, my people; remember, Israel.
For you were sold to the nations, but not for destruction. Because you angered God, you were handed over to your enemies.
For you angered your Creator: you sacrificed to demons and not to God.
You forgot the eternal God who nourished you, and you grieved Jerusalem, who nursed you.
For she saw the wrath from God that had come upon you, and said, “Listen, exiles of Zion, for the Lord has brought great mourning upon me.
I saw the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Eternal One brought upon them.
I raised them with joy, but sent them away with weeping and mourning.
Let no one trample on me, a widow who has been left alone. I have been deprived of many because of the many sins of my children, for they turned away from the laws of God.
They did not know his ordinances, did not walk in the ways of God's commandments, and did not follow the paths of instruction in his righteousness.
Let the strangers in Zion come and remember the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Eternal One brought upon them.
He brought upon them a distant nation, a shameless nation speaking another language.
They showed no respect for the old and no mercy to the young. They took away the loved ones of me, a widow, and left me bereft of my daughters.
And I, for my part, was unable to help you.
May the one who brought these calamities upon you rescue you from the hands of your enemies.
Go, my children, go, for I have been left desolate.
I took off the robe of peace and put on the sackcloth of my supplications. I cried out to the Eternal One throughout my days.
Take courage, children; cry out to God, and he will rescue you from the oppression of your enemies’ hands.
For I placed my hope in the Eternal One for your salvation, and joy came to me from the Holy One because of the mercy that will soon come to you from the Eternal One, your Savior.
For I sent you away with mourning and weeping, but may God give you back to me with gladness and joy forever.
For just as the strangers in Zion have now seen your captivity, so they will soon see your salvation from God, which will come upon you with great glory and radiance from the Eternal One.
My children, patiently endure the wrath that has come upon you from God. Your enemy persecuted you, but you will soon see his destruction and step on his neck.
My pampered ones traveled rough roads; they were driven away like a flock seized by enemies.
Take courage, my children, and cry out to God, so that you may be remembered by [?].
For just as your minds went astray from God, turn back and seek him with ten times greater zeal.
For the one who brought calamities upon you will bring you everlasting joy, together with comfort for you.
Take courage, Jerusalem. The one who named you will comfort you.
Woe to the one who afflicted you and to those who rejoiced at your destruction.
Woe to the cities where your children served, and woe to the one that received your sons.
For just as she rejoiced at your destruction and was glad at your fall, so she will grieve over her own devastation.
I will take away from her the joy of her many celebrations and turn her splendor into mourning.
Fire from the Eternal One will come upon her for many days, and she will be a dwelling place of demons for a long time.
Look to the east, Jerusalem, and see the joy coming to you from God.
Look, your sons whom you sent away are coming. They come gathered from the east to the west at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.
Take off your garment of mourning and lamentation, Jerusalem, and put on the beauty of God's glory forever.
Wrap yourself in the robe of righteousness from God; place on your head the crown of the glory of the Eternal One.
For God will show all your splendor under heaven.
And God will give you this name forever: “Peace of righteousness and glory of godliness.”
Rise, Jerusalem, and stand on the heights. Look toward the east and see your children gathered from east to west at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing that God has remembered them.
For they went away from you on foot, driven by enemies, but God will bring them back to you, carried high in glory as on a royal throne.
For God has commanded every high mountain and the everlasting hills to be lowered, and the valleys to be filled to make the earth level, so that Israel may walk safely in the glory of God.
And all forests and every fragrant tree will shade Israel at God's command.

For God will lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory, with mercy and righteousness that come from him.

Baruch
